wci.headline: WCI decreased 3% for the fourth consecutive week. See detailed commentary below.
wci.text_en:
Our detailed assessment for Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
The Drewry World Container Index (WCI), the benchmark widely referenced by procurement teams, decreased 3% to $4,176 per 40ft container this week due to declining rates on the Transpacific trade route. Despite the decline, the WCI remains 126% higher YoY.
On the Transpacific trade route, rates continued their downwards trend for the seventh consecutive week. Rates from Shanghai to New York decreased 9% to $8,194 per 40ft container, the lowest in 15 weeks, and those from Shanghai to Los Angeles fell 5% to $7,026 per 40ft container, the lowest in 12 weeks. In response to the weak demand, carriers are reducing capacity through blank sailings. According to Drewry's
Container Capacity Insight , ten blank sailings have been announced for next week, compared with four this week. Despite these capacity reductions, Drewry expects freight rates to decrease further next week.
On the Asia-Europe/Med trade route, rates from Shanghai to Genoa increased 6% to $4,436 per 40ft container after remaining stable for three consecutive weeks, while Shanghai to Rotterdam rates remained unchanged at $3,496 per 40ft container. Carriers are managing capacity through blank sailings, and according to Drewry’s
Container Capacity Insight , four blank sailings are announced for next week, lower than five this week. As demand is expected to strengthen in December ahead of the new contract season, many carriers have announced PSS, ranging from $1,000-1,600 per 40ft container on Asia-Europe/Med effective December. Hence, Drewry expects rates to increase in the coming weeks.
The East-West container shipping market remains under pressure, with different trends on Transpacific and Asia-Europe/Med trade routes. Asia–Europe demand is expected to strengthen in December ahead of the new contract season and Chinese New Year, prompting carriers to push rate increases through surcharges, whereas easing Transpacific demand is likely to drive rates lower. Meanwhile, worsening North Europe port congestion is delaying empty-container returns to Asia, raising concerns over future equipment shortages. Suez Canal transits improved to 57 vessels last week, while only four vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz. With geopolitical uncertainty and potential labour disruptions at Los Angeles and Long Beach remain key risks, shippers should expect continued rate volatility.

Container Freight Rate Insight  for a comprehensive fortnightly & monthly picture of spot market freight rates across 6,700 port pairs. Includes analysis of market developments and the key factors shaping costs across the major trade routes.
paragraphs: 19 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla Drewry Dünya Konteyner Endeksi (WCI), Transpasifik hattındaki düşüşün etkisiyle %3 azalarak 40'lık konteyner başına 4.176 dolara geriledi. Transpasifik hattında zayıf talep nedeniyle düşüş sürerken, Şanghay–New York hattı %9 azalışla 8.194 dolara, Şanghay–Los Angeles hattı ise %5 düşüşle 7.026 dolara indi. Buna karşın Asya–Avrupa hattında Şanghay–Cenova navlun fiyatları %6 artarak 4.436 dolara çıkarken, Şanghay–Rotterdam hattı 3.496 dolar seviyesinde sabit kaldı.

Aralık ayında yeni sözleşme sezonu ve Çin Yeni Yılı öncesinde talebin güçlenmesi beklenirken, taşıyıcılar ek ücretler uygulamaya hazırlanıyor. Kuzey Avrupa limanlarındaki tıkanıklık boş konteyner iadelerini geciktirirken, Süveyş Kanalı geçişleri 57 gemiye yükseldi. Drewry, zayıflayan Transpasifik talebi nedeniyle önümüzdeki hafta navlun fiyatlarının daha da düşmesini bekliyor.
